mission_02: Think of the date range as two boundaries: the first day of 2025 and the first day of 2026. You need a lower bound and an upper bound.
Use `>= '2025-01-01'` for the lower bound and `< '2026-01-01'` for the upper bound. The upper bound uses `<` on the first day of the next year so no 2026 rows leak in.
The rule of thumb: never wrap an indexed column in a function in a WHERE clause. Instead, express the condition as a range on the bare column.
